notes: OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens Standard (29 CFR 1910.1030) final rule published Dec 6, 1991: year 1991 correct (revised 2001 for needlestick safety).
Three-level ladder and 'only sterilization kills spores' consistent with CDC (low/intermediate-level disinfection is not sporicidal). 'Disinfection kills most germs' is an acceptable simplification.
'Standard Precautions' is the CDC term; OSHA's term is universal precautions. Acceptable.
Epidermis avascular, dermis holds vessels/nerves/glands/follicles/collagen, subcutaneous fat layer, melanocytes in basal layer, trigeminal (V) sensory and facial (VII) motor: all correct.
BCC most common and rarely metastasizes; melanoma most dangerous: confirmed. Tinea, impetigo, scabies contagious: correct. Lesion classifications correct.

Anagen/catagen/telogen correct; roughly 85-95% of scalp hairs in anagen supports 'most'. OSHA HazCom (29 CFR 1910.1200) revision effective 2012 (GHS aligned); employers must keep an SDS for each hazardous chemical used: correct. Volt/amp/ohm correct.

Fitzpatrick Type I is commonly stated as 'always burns, never tans' (chapter says 'rarely tans'; minor, not wrong for a teaching summary). Type VI never burns: correct. Wood's lamp: yellow=oily, purple=dehydrated/dry in common esthetic teaching: consistent.

Five massage movements and AHA (water-soluble, surface) vs BHA/salicylic (oil-soluble) correct. Facial step order varies by textbook (extraction vs massage order); acceptable as stated. Enzymes listed as chemical exfoliant: commonly grouped so.
Wax applied with growth, removed against growth parallel to skin for both hard and soft wax: confirmed. Patch test 24-48 h: consistent with industry guidance.

FDA statement: FDA has not approved any color additive for permanent dyeing of lashes/brows; strictly, FDA approved silver nitrate (up to 4%, professional use, brows only, not lashes). Chapter wording is close to FDA's own phrasing; optional nuance 'permanent dyeing'.
Regrowth 'slower vs faster' (epilation vs depilation) is common exam teaching; science says shaving does not change growth rate, only blunt tips feel stubbly. Minor.
SPF primarily measures UVB; broad spectrum = UVA proportional to UVB (FDA): correct. Humectant/emollient/occlusive definitions and examples correct. Color wheel statements correct.
